before we begin every child brings different strengths, needs, and ways of participating. creating an inclusive environment starts with noticing barriers and being willing to adapt. notice recognize barriers that may affect participation, communication, or belonging. adapt explore practical ways to adjust activities, environments, and communication. include practice making thoughtful choices that help every child participate. you don't need to have all the answers. you just need to be willing to notice, listen, and adapt. meet maya meet maya meet maya meet maya meet maya meet maya

small changes can make an activity more accessible. families and children can help you understand what supports participation. start by noticing what is happening—not by assuming why. maya enjoys discovering new things. giving children opportunities to explore can support curiosity and independent participation. maya enjoys puzzles and activities that allow her to work at her own pace. maya enjoys stories and picture books. story-based activities can also give children a predictable way to engage with a group. stories stories stories stories puzzles puzzles puzzles puzzles exploring exploring exploring exploring meet maya maya is a 4 year-old scout who is interested in: ask ask 2 ask before you meet maya your challenge maya often watches before joining. maya stays near the edge while the group prepares for a busy game. how could you help maya, and every chipmunk, participate? observe observe 1 observe 1 1 adapt adapt 3 adapt let’s find out let’s find out let’s find out let’s find out let’s find out let’s find out 2 2 3 3

accessibility means removing barriers so every child can participate, communicate, learn, play, and belong. for young children, barriers can show up in the environment, activities, communication, routines, sensory experiences, social interactions, or expectations. what does “accessibility” actually mean? what does this mean for early years children? → “ accessibility refers to the design of products, devices, services, or environments for people who experience disabilities.” accessibility service canada “accessibility is enabling persons with disabilities to live independently and participate fully in all aspects of life, having access to all aspects of society on an equal and equitable basis with others united nations.” convention on the rights of persons with disabilities “accessibility is about addressing environmental barriers that hinder people's full and effective participation.” world health organization, disability and health
